approved_slide.file: 73. Procurement and Supplier Collaboration Agent one-pager.pptx

findings: New catalog template authored from an internal eight-step use-case outline for procurement and supplier collaboration; no prior library source covered competitive sourcing of network materials through invoice match.
The outline used a cloud AI service for bid evaluation; library solutions use only Copilot Studio, Microsoft 365, Power Platform and Dynamics 365.

The Purchase Order Management and Procurement Savings agents cover software and vendor-contract buying, and the Supplier Claim Engagement Agent covers retail claims; none covers routes, RFQs, bid scoring, ASNs or three-way match.
Issuing RFQs, answering bidders, awarding, ordering and approving payment are external actions and must not run from a synthetic template.
fixes: Authored a single-file, stdlib-only agent with 5 deterministic operations covering the eight steps over an invented utility snapshot behind one marked data-plane seam.

Mapped requisitions, orders, receipts and invoices to Dataverse tables filled by Power Automate from the ERP, the supplier portal to Power Apps, and bid scoring to transparent published weights in Copilot Studio.
Answered supplier questions only from the published RFQ pack and routed anything new to a clarification for every bidder, so no bidder gets an advantage.
Represented every route, reply, award, order, message and payment as a labeled draft or recommendation with an explicit no-action gate; dates are relative to the run date.
Used only a fictional utility, suppliers, people and identifiers.
Added one locked persona-language case and one uploadable skill per operation.
remaining_boundary: Production connections and all external actions require customer approval, least-privilege controls, authenticated supplier access, and an authorized human workflow. Bid scores are decision support; the award panel decides.
